issues.legal_issue: An amendment extending an existing compulsory-acquisition law to additional categories of property is protected from fundamental-rights challenge when the amendment receives presidential assent.
material_facts: The original law provided for abolition and vesting of estates for a public purpose.
The amendment widened the definition of estate to cover additional property, including minor inams, and extended the existing abolition scheme to that property.
The amendment was reserved for presidential consideration and received the President’s assent.
issues.conclusion: The amendment was valid and protected by Article 31A; presidential assent to the amendment extended the protection to the newly covered categories of property.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31A(1) protects laws providing for acquisition of estates or rights therein from challenges under Articles 14, 19 and 31, subject, for a State law, to presidential assent. Article 31A(2)(a) includes inams within the meaning of estate. The Court treated an amendment extending an existing acquisition law as an extension of that law, to which the President’s assent applies; it also considered the assent requirement under Article 31 and the effect of Article 31(4). No earlier cases are relied on in the supplied judgment.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_property_acq: The affected property holders brought a constitutional challenge to a law providing for acquisition of property.
predicates.amendment_extends_existing_acquisition_l: The legislature amended an existing acquisition law to extend its operation to additional categories of property.
predicates.existing_law_provides_compulsory_acquisi: The existing law provides for compulsory acquisition of property for a public purpose.
predicates.amendment_received_presidential_assent: The amendment was reserved for presidential consideration and received the President’s assent.

issues.definition: When property holders constitutionally challenge an amendment extending an existing public-purpose acquisition law, and the amendment received presidential assent, the amendment is protected.

issues.legal_issue: Minor inams are estates subject to abolition and vesting where the governing definition covers any inam, even if the grant concerns land rather than a whole village and includes both landholding rights.
material_facts: The appellants held pre-settlement minor inams granted over particular lands rather than whole villages.
The grants comprised both the melwaram and kudiwaram rights.
The amended definition of estate included any inam, and the State issued a notification declaring the relevant estate vested in it.
issues.conclusion: The minor inams fell within the amended definition of estate and could be vested in the State under the abolition law; the notification was valid.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31A(2)(a) includes any inam within the meaning of estate. The amended definition in section 2(g) of the Orissa Estates Abolition Act covered the minor inams, so the residual definition provision in section 2(q) and the definition in the Madras Estates Land Act did not restrict that express coverage. Under section 3, a notification covering an estate within the definition causes it to vest in the State. Article 31A protects the law from the specified fundamental-rights challenges.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_estate_vesting and grant_is_an_inam and amended_definition_covers_any_inam and government_issued_vesting_notification

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_estate_vesti: Property holders challenged the application of an estate-vesting law and notification to their property.
predicates.grant_is_an_inam: The property consisted of a grant recognized as an inam, although it covered particular lands rather than a whole village.
predicates.amended_definition_covers_any_inam: The governing amended definition expressly covers any inam, without limiting the term to grants of whole villages.
predicates.government_issued_vesting_notification: The government issued a notification declaring the covered estate vested in the State.

issues.definition: Where a constitutional challenge concerns an inam grant covered by the governing definition and the government has issued a vesting notification, the grant is subject to vesting.

issues.legal_issue: The ejusdem generis rule does not restrict an expressly listed category such as inam by reference to the other listed categories, although it may inform the meaning of a following phrase covering other similar grants.
material_facts: The constitutional definition of estate expressly listed jagir, inam and muafi, followed by the phrase other similar grant.
The appellants argued that the ejusdem generis rule should restrict the meaning of inam.
issues.conclusion: The ejusdem generis rule did not restrict the express inclusion of inam; it could apply to the phrase other similar grant.
issues.legal_principle: The ejusdem generis rule may cut down a general term by reference to the genus of specific terms preceding it. The Court held that the rule does not restrict specific categories expressly included in a definition, but may apply to the general phrase other similar grant, which takes its colour from the preceding categories.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_estate_defin: Property holders challenged the interpretation of a definition in a constitutional appeal.
predicates.definition_expressly_lists_inam: The definition expressly names inam as an included category.
predicates.general_similar_grant_phrase_follows_lis: The definition places a general phrase covering similar grants after its specifically named categories.

issues.definition: When a definition expressly lists inam before a general phrase for similar grants, the listed category is not restricted by the ejusdem generis rule.
